note: Every chapter epigraph is Louis Segond (1910) verbatim, cited with the French book name and no version label (as in a-retrospect-teens.fr); where the English KJV quotes part of a verse, the matching Segond portion is used (1 Cor 8:1b, Jas 1:19b starting at Segond's « Ainsi, », Matt 6:6a, 1 Cor 10:13a, John 15:15a, Prov 24:16a). Segond's line-initial capitals and its unaccented « A celui » (Isa 26:3) are kept as printed. Ch. 3 quotes John 21:22 with Segond's opening clause (« Si je veux qu’il demeure… ») so the short reply reads naturally.

All of Thomas's own sentences are taken word for word from the shipped full edition (the-imitation-of-christ.fr), cut only where the English cuts, so the full and teen editions read as one book; this includes the Book III address « mon fils » for the English 'child' (ch. 12), and ch. 1's John 8:12 and Ecclesiastes 1:8, which follow that edition's wording and are self_rendered. Ch. 5 re-persons « il est humilié, purifié et instruit » to « nous sommes humiliés, purifiés et instruits » as the English does.

Names follow the full edition: Thomas a Kempis (unaccented, French usage), mont Sainte-Agnès, Frères de la Vie commune. The title « L’Imitation de Jésus-Christ (Pour ados) » (39 characters) is built on the full edition's title as instructed and exceeds the 28-character target; « L’Imitation (Pour ados) » would be the short fallback. Ch. 10 glosses « d’une âme égale » in place of the English gloss of 'equanimity'; ch. 11 drops the gloss of 'eventide', since « le soir venu » needs none.

Short Gospel echoes worded exactly as Segond are marked mined (Matt 6:34 in ch. 11, Matt 20:16 and 20:28 in ch. 12, « le pain de vie » John 6:35 in ch. 13); a reviewer may prefer to treat them as self_rendered. AI-translated in-session; awaiting native review.
